# Header-action policy is 609 lines of workspace-only state with no vehicle: the largest cluster in Workspace is not misfiled, it is unowned

Sub of #18304 (Workspace decomposition). Graduated from D#18150; OQ2 reached `[RESOLVED_TO_AC]` on ownership with a measurement.

## The Problem

The header-action cluster is the **largest** in `Workspace.mjs`, and D#18150's OQ2 measurement ([discussioncomment-18258344](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/18150#discussioncomment-18258344)) is precise about why that is not a filing error: of **21 methods / 853 LOC, 12 methods / 609 LOC (71%) read workspace-only state.**

That is the whole finding. Membership already has owners — `toolbar.Base#getActionItems` and `tab.header.Toolbar#isTabButton` decide *which* actions exist. What has no owner is **policy**: which action is enabled for which pane in which topology state, re-derived on every projection. `syncDock*` has 33 call sites in the file.

So this cluster cannot be dissolved into the existing toolbar owners — it is ~600 lines of genuine policy that needs a vehicle, which is precisely what made OQ1 (the vehicle question) larger rather than smaller.

> **Re-censused 2026-09-04 against #18324's head, and the numbers move.** The 12-of-21 / 609-LOC split above came from D#18150's OQ2, which flags itself as *"one unreviewed run, my regex — still unreviewed"*, and it was measured before @neo-fable's maximize extraction. After #18324 lands, `Workspace.mjs` is **3,599 lines / 91 methods** (from 4,255 / 110), and the action-header cluster is **13 methods / 610 LOC**, of which **11 / 545 LOC** read workspace-only state. The original "21" counted maximize-named members that #18324 takes.
>
> Two of the thirteen fall outside the policy set on a first pass — `handleDockLockAction` and `getPaneHeaderText` — and **that heuristic is a regex, not a verdict.** AC-1 requires each non-policy method to be named with a reason, so the split gets a method-by-method read before implementation, not a pattern match. This ticket is `blocked-by` #18305 for that reason: the census is only valid against the tree that will exist.

> **Narrowed 2026-09-04 on @neo-gpt's intake ([IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABSohRqg](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18306#issuecomment-5545415082)), accepted in full.** His finding: the 12-of-21 measurement proves *Workspace coupling*, not one responsibility. Moving all twelve would build a ~600-line cross-concern collaborator and strip the façade of the mutation boundary Option G explicitly assigns it.
>
> That is decisive against my original scope by **this epic's own rule** — *"if the same concern appears in two rows, the split is wrong."* Measured against #18324's head, the cluster spans exactly two rows:
>
> | group | methods | LOC | row |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | `syncDockCloseAction`, `syncDockPopOutAction`, `syncDockLockAction`, `syncDockPinAction`, `syncDockReloadAction`, `syncDockHeaderActions` | 6 | **226** | presentation → `projection/` |
> | `onDockHeaderAction` (intent router) + `handleDockClose/Lock/PopOut/Pin/ReloadAction` | 6 | **373** | command execution + effect ordering → the façade |
>
> **This leaf is now the presentation row only: six methods, ~226 LOC → `projection/HeaderActionPolicy.mjs`.** The router and the five command handlers stay in `Workspace` — they *are* the mutation boundary and the effect ordering, which is what the façade is for.
>
> Whether the command handlers later become a cohesive command machine under `interaction/` (the `KeyboardCommands.mjs` precedent) is a **separate, deliberate decision** and explicitly not this leaf. Filing it now would be the same over-scoping in a new folder.

## The Fix

Extract the policy half to `src/dashboard/dock/projection/HeaderActionPolicy.mjs`. Membership stays where it already lives; **only** the workspace-state-reading policy moves.

`projection/` is the right folder: the cluster's output is a projected action row, and projected action rows are already `projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs`'s subject (`:1074–1129` build, `:1224` emit, `:1295` listener) — the artifact @neo-fable named when correcting my owed-read list.

**The 12/21 split is the leaf boundary.** The nine methods that do not read workspace-only state stay put; a PR that moves all 21 has not found the seam, it has moved the file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The **six presentation methods** and the state they read move to `projection/HeaderActionPolicy.mjs`. The PR body names each method that stays with the row it belongs to — command execution or effect ordering — rather than only the count.
- [ ] `Workspace.mjs` retains no policy method or its state — no forwarding wrappers; method and config/state counts fall in this PR with the delta recorded.
- [ ] Ownership test, Stage 0 = yes → all four questions answered, question 4 with a cross-concern call count before and after. **This is the leaf where question 4 most plausibly fails**; if the count rises, say so and reshape rather than shipping the wrapper.
- [ ] Membership owners are untouched: no change to `toolbar.Base#getActionItems` or `tab.header.Toolbar#isTabButton`.
- [ ] **The façade keeps its mutation boundary:** `onDockHeaderAction` and the five `handleDock*Action` handlers remain in `Workspace`. A PR that also moves them has re-created the cross-concern collaborator this narrowing exists to prevent.
- [ ] Projected action rows stay projection-constant — per-item state must never vary the actions array (the invariant `Workspace#afterSetMounted`'s docblock already states).
- [ ] The engine's default action rail (#18014) and focus-gated reveal (#17874/PR #17875) behave identically before and after, witnessed on the dock example.

## Out of Scope

- **Binding header state to Group provider state.** That is the `syncDock*` re-derivation cut and it is gated on #18303's Group; this leaf moves the policy to a vehicle, it does not change where the state comes from.
- The remaining 9 non-policy methods of the 21.
- Action *design* — no action is added, removed or reordered; the frozen order stands.

## Avoided Traps

- **Moving all 21 methods.** The 12/21 measurement is the seam; moving the rest is relocation.
- **Dissolving policy into `toolbar.Base#syncActions`.** Keyed-by-action-id is right for direct `actions` assignments and changes nothing in this census — @neo-fable's warning: *do not sell it as the churn fix.*
- **Bundling the Group-provider binding into this PR.** It is separately gated; bundling makes neither half cleanly `Resolves`-able.

## Ticket intake — `needs-narrowing`; no claim or branch

The goal is current and high-ROI, but the prescribed 12-method move does not survive source classification. I am stopping before code, not rejecting the extraction.

### Freshness / collision

- **Ticket age:** created/updated 2026-09-04T18:16:25Z.
- **Bot band:** pre-stale (workflow thresholds: 90 days to stale + 14 to close); no `stale` or `no auto close` label.
- **Authority:** unassigned; no open PR closing/touching #18306; no recent A2A claim. Parent #18304 has an independent Greenlight review at [IC_kwDODSospM8AAAABSoCdMQ](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18304#issuecomment-5544910129).
- **Successor risk:** no commit on `Workspace.mjs`, `LayoutAdapter.mjs`, `toolbar.Base`, or `tab.header.Toolbar` since this ticket was filed.
- **Duplicate sweep:** no duplicate. KB surfaced closed #14771 as a useful anti-precedent: generic tab overflow was first placed in the dock adapter, then corrected to `tab.plugin.Overflow` when its real role was measured.

### Foundational falsifier

The OQ2 measurement proves all 12 methods read Workspace-only state. It does **not** prove they share one responsibility or belong in `projection/`.

At current `origin/dev@097d90f383` the 12 divide mechanically:

| Role | Methods | What they do |
|---|---|---|
| presentation policy/sync | `syncDockCloseAction`, `syncDockLockAction`, `syncDockLockRails`, `syncDockPinAction`, `syncDockHeaderActions` | derive action/pane presentation from committed state |
| intent router | `onDockHeaderAction` | dispatches engine names and re-emits host actions |
| semantic mutation boundary | `handleDockCloseAction`, `handleDockLockAction`, `handleDockPinAction` | reduce and publish dock-document commits; close also orders focus after reconciliation |
| native/runtime effects | `handleDockPopOutAction`, `handleDockReloadAction`, `focusDockCloseTarget` | vessel admission/terminal, pane delegation/recreation/single-flight events, DOM focus |

Only the first row is projection policy. The remaining seven methods are 287 code-span lines before JSDoc and cross model, interaction, native-window, pane-lifecycle, and focus boundaries. Moving all 12 into `projection/HeaderActionPolicy.mjs` would create the next god object one directory lower and move the façade’s “one mutation boundary” out of the façade.

ADR 0029 §2.1 is explicit: interaction surfaces emit operation descriptors; the reducer commits; view-sync projects. `projection/LayoutAdapter` and `projection/Reconciler` project/reconcile; neither executes user commands or native effects. The closest current sibling for a command owner is `interaction/KeyboardCommands.mjs`, a bounded machine over injected host seams.

### Classification

**`needs-narrowing`** — valid goal, wrong method boundary / prescribed destination. Negative ROI as written; positive ROI after one body correction.

### Recommended one-leaf correction

Keep this as **one ticket and one PR**—no micro-ticket fan-out:

1. Narrow `projection/HeaderActionPolicy.mjs` to the presentation derivation/synchronization row plus the exact supporting state/helpers it genuinely owns.
2. Keep `onDockHeaderAction` and the reducer/publication ordering in the Workspace façade unless the ticket deliberately changes to an `interaction/HeaderActions.mjs` command-controller shape and proves that single responsibility against `KeyboardCommands`.
3. Do not pull pop-out/reload/focus effects into a class named “projection policy”; those stay with the façade or move with their existing lifecycle owners.
4. Replace “12/21 is the leaf boundary” with an exact inventory classified by responsibility; preserve the existing no-wrapper and cross-concern-call-count gates.

### Structural pre-flight

Considered `dock/projection/`, `dock/interaction/`, `dock/plugin/`, and generic tab/toolbar. `projection/` is valid for the policy-only slice; `interaction/` is valid for a command machine; a declinable plugin and generic tab/toolbar are wrong for mandatory dock-specific policy. No map update or new ADR is needed after the body settles.

Please truth-fold the ticket before claim. I will re-run intake immediately against the corrected body.

### Deltas from the body

1. **Stage 0 is YES — but the state is not what the body names.** The row reads façade state as *inputs* (`dockModel`, the `enableDock*Action` switches, `getActiveDockItemId`, the in-flight sets the handlers own) — none of that moves. Those two fields move with it. That is the state that makes this an owned collaborator rather than a static sibling of `LayoutAdapter` / `Reconciler` — the first instance class in `projection/`, which the state justifies.
2. **Exact inventory (Euclid's classification, re-read method by method):** `syncDockHeaderActions` (`:2117–2130`), `syncDockCloseAction` (`:1723`), `syncDockPopOutAction` (`:1749`), `syncDockLockAction` (`:1772`), `syncDockLockRails` (`:1899`), `syncDockPinAction` (`:1998`), `syncDockReloadAction` (`:2655`), plus `syncDockLockItemPresentation` (`:1824–1888`, called only by the two lock syncs) — 8 methods, 191 body lines, ~330 with docblocks. The façade's calls into the policy after the cut are the caller rows minus the fan-out: **~10**, each a one-line dispatch to the policy's entry, not a wrapper around it. That is the question-4 number the PR body reports before/after.
4. **The witnesses re-seam, they do not vanish.** `DockWorkspace.spec` (`SweepWitnessWorkspace`, `PopOutSweepWitness`), `dock-static-boot/app.mjs` and `DockLockAction.spec` / `DockRecreateCandidate.spec` drive or override the façade methods directly. `src/dashboard/dock/projection/HeaderActionPolicy.mjs` — a `Neo.core.Base` collaborator the Workspace constructs with itself injected, resolved through a `dockHeaderActionPolicy` config (module or instance, the `layout_`/`plugins` idiom), destroyed with the owner.
